adversarial_review.check: The finite oscillator is explicitly a regularization and no exact CCR/domain conclusion is drawn.
The onsite and bond coefficients are read from the registered Q3 model; no production owner is substituted.
The cosine taper is fully declared and is tested only at finite n and finite L.
The full-H Gibbs state and both right/left seminorm legs are retained separately.
delta_H uses the same full H as rho; no modular/Hamiltonian identification beyond finite type I is claimed.
Four oscillator sizes are a stress test only; no dimension or volume limit is inferred.
The second script reconstructs the matrices without importing the primary implementation and agrees within 1e-7.
R262 checks rational algebra and scope only, not floating-point exponentials or unbounded limits.
OS/KMS/GNS, common alpha, gap, continuum, C6, Sector A and Pre-A remain open.

boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite regularized Q3 structured-cutoff audit; no thermodynamic or OS/KMS/GNS closure.
decision_reason: This is genuine QFT-facing progress because the matrices use the actual registered Q3 onsite and bond, the Gibbs state is generated by the same full Hamiltonian, and the two-sided GNS seminorm plus Hamiltonian modular derivative are measured directly. It is not a thermodynamic theorem: finite oscillator matrices do not preserve the exact CCR, no lattice-volume sequence or common representation is supplied, and the observed ratios are diagnostics rather than a uniformity proof or counterexample.
finding: The primary lane passes 212/212 and the independent lane passes 162/162. The integrated verifier passes 94/94 with Lean R262 PASS. The static two-sided tail decreases over the declared radii for every n and remains above the numerical floor. The largest observed D/(|t|*tail) ratio is approximately 0.388456 and the largest observed modular-derivative/tail ratio is approximately 1.485492. The modular companion is therefore a separate load-bearing estimate even in this finite Q3 regularization; the four finite dimensions do not establish a dimension- or volume-uniform constant.
method: Build the two-site truncated oscillator q and p matrices and the registered quartic onsite plus quadratic/cubic Q3 bond with chi=1, r=-1, g=3/5, c=1 and lambda=1/10.
Use the full-H Gibbs state at beta=1 and the bounded configuration character exp(i*q_1/4).
Replace each q by the declared cosine-taper spectral cutoff q_L, construct H_L, and compute the full-versus-cutoff Heisenberg difference D_L(t) for t in {1/10,1/5}.
Evaluate both sides of N_beta,#(D)^2 and N_beta,#(delta_H D)^2, check the configuration-commutation cancellation at t=0, and repeat for oscillator sizes n=4,6,8,10 and radii L={3/4,1,5/4,3/2}.
Rebuild the matrix calculation in a separate numerical lane and compile Lean R262 for the rational fixture algebra and scope firewall.
next_action: Derive an analytic mixed force-momentum estimate on the common Q3 form core that explains the finite modular ratios and either supplies a dimension/volume-uniform constant or exposes a true scaling obstruction.
no_overclaim: This is a finite QFT-facing diagnostic only. It is not an all-time projected D/delta-D theorem, an OS reconstruction, a KMS/GNS result, a mass-gap proof, a continuum result, a C6/Sector-A/Pre-A result, a TECT production map or a Clay result.
